overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: the December 5 notice adequately described the tax classification hearing, and signing the tax form during a recess after the vote was administrative. Separate hearing-law claims were declined.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the December 5 meeting notice topic on the tax classification hearing did not indicate it was a public hearing.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the topic as posted provided the public with sufficient detail about the hearing, including the fact that it was indeed a hearing

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board formally adopted the tax classifications during a recess of the meeting rather than during the open meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Because the Board had already voted on the tax classifications during its meeting and took a recess for the sole purpose of digitally signing the tax rate recapitulation form, its actions during the recess did not violate the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board failed to properly open and close the public hearing and gave insufficient time for public review and comment on the tax classifications.
allegations.key_passage: we decline to review, and offer no opinion on, whether there was a violation of any separate hearing law
